title: Spatial scene
description: A worm's-eye photo of a wooden pole under summer cumulus that turns out to have depth, and room above it. It fills the screen, cropped edge to edge. Look up and you crouch in to the foot of the pole as the camera pitches up and the lens opens from the photo's crop to a stereographic 116 degrees: the foot flares off the bottom of the frame, the shaft converges on the zenith, and the sky opens into a deep cobalt dome the photo never showed, its clouds carried on past the photo's edges. Look sideways and the camera turns round the pole, so the wires and the cloud behind them slide apart. The sky was baked offline as its own layer at infinity, inpainted behind the pole and wires and continued into a whole sky dome; the pole is a mesh displaced by its own depth, and the wires run on past the photo as lines in 3D.
intent: Apple's Spatial Scenes (iOS 26 lock screen and Photos, https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/spatial-scenes) and Facebook 3D Photos (2018, https://ai.meta.com/blog/powered-by-ai-turning-any-2d-photo-into-3d-using-convolutional-neural-nets/): a flat photo you know suddenly has depth that behaves correctly, foreground sliding over background that was hidden behind it.
